tip: Welsh puts the need on you. Mae angen moddion arna i is literally medicine is a need on me, meaning I need medicine.
mynd yn plus an adjective means becoming. Here mynd yn hirach means getting longer, not simply going somewhere.
Mae'n well gen i means I prefer, literally it is better with me, so mae'n well gen i gerdded is I prefer walking.
Pa, meaning which, softens the next consonant, so llwybr becomes lwybr in Pa lwybr, which path.
For a real if, Welsh uses Os with a future verb. Os gorffenna i means if I finish, then bydda i, I will.
Byddwn i wedi galw means I would have called. Pair it with pe bawn i, if I were, for the unreal past condition.
Mae'n gas gen i means I hate, literally it is hateful with me, so mae'n gas gen i smocio is I hate smoking.
The ending ach makes comparatives, so anodd, hard, becomes anoddach, harder, in Mae Cymraeg yn anoddach.
Fronting a subject adds emphasis. Y fferm sy ger y llyn means it is the farm that is near the lake.
After llawer o, lots of, the next word softens, so pethau becomes bethau in llawer o bethau.
yn hytrach na means rather than. Byddai'n well gen i gerdded yn hytrach na gyrru is I'd rather walk than drive.
Pe baen nhw means if they had, and bydden nhw wedi helpu means they would have helped, the unreal past pattern.
Welsh weather uses bwrw, to cast. Bwrw eira literally casts snow and means to snow, as in Os bydd hi'n bwrw eira.
To bring is dod â, literally come with. Mae'r gwanwyn yn dod â'r ŵyn means spring brings the lambs.
The object of a short-form verb softens, so pysgod, fish, becomes bysgod in Bwyton ni bysgod.
His here is 'i, tucked after the verb, and it softens crys to grys in smwddio'i grys, ironing his shirt.
